title: Is McDonald's Actually a Real Estate Company?
description:
McDonald's collected $10.4 billion in rent from its franchisees in 2025, more than all the food sold in its own restaurants, and the plan goes back to a 1950s finance chief.
#mcdonalds #realestate #business #shorts

Sources: McDonald's Corporation 2025 Form 10-K; McDonald's Q3 2026 results (Nov 2026); AP via KPTV (Nov 4, 2026); SABR biography of Ray Kroc; Entrepreneur; Footnote Brief, citing John F. Love's McDonald's: Behind the Arches; Wall Street Survivor
Photos: nayukim, milst1, Tony Fischer Photography, bradleygee, dave_mcmt, pasa47, Clotee Pridgen Allochuku, zigazou76 (CC BY 2.0, Flickr)
tags: is mcdonalds a real estate company
first_comment: Be honest: would you rather own a McDonald's, or the land under it? 🍔🏠

scenes.say: McDonald's isn't really a burger company. Last year it made {$10.4 BILLION|ten point four billion dollars} from rent.
scenes.source: McDonald's 2025 Form 10-K, Franchise Arrangements note: Rents $10,442M (2025); Footnote Brief (2024 rents $10.02B, same pattern)

scenes.say: Rent beat all the food sold in its own restaurants, which came to {$9.7 BILLION|nine point seven billion dollars}.
scenes.source: McDonald's 2025 10-K: sales by Company-owned and operated restaurants $9,690M; rents $10,442M (largest revenue line; total revenues $26,885M). Footnote Brief: 2024 rents $10.02B vs company-operated sales $9.78B

scenes.say: It started in the {1950s|fifties}. Ray Kroc kept just {1.4%|one point four percent} of each restaurant's sales.
scenes.source: Encyclopedia.com, McDonald, Mac & Dick ('1.9 percent, of which Kroc would get 1.4 percent and the brothers would get 0.5 percent'); SABR biography of Ray Kroc ('1.9 percent of the gross sales'); Entrepreneur

scenes.say: Then a finance guy named Harry Sonneborn said: buy the land first.
scenes.source: Wikipedia, Harry J. Sonneborn and History of McDonald's (Franchise Realty Corp); Entrepreneur ('suggested he earn money by selling real estate'); Footnote Brief (Franchise Realty, 1957)

scenes.say: Rent it to the {franchisee|franchise owner}. And charge more as their sales grow.
scenes.source: Entrepreneur ('a set monthly rental for the land or a percentage of their sales, whichever was greater'); McDonald's 2025 10-K ('rent and royalties based on a percent of sales with minimum rent payments')

scenes.say: As he reportedly put it: we are not technically in the food business. We are in the real estate business.
scenes.source: Footnote Brief, citing John F. Love, McDonald's: Behind the Arches; Wall Street Survivor; Sam Sawyer (Substack)

scenes.say: But here's the interesting part: it still owns the land under {56%|fifty six percent} of its restaurants in its main markets.
scenes.source: McDonald's 2025 10-K ('owned approximately 56% of the land and approximately 80% of the buildings for restaurants in its consolidated markets'); Footnote Brief (land under about 45% of all restaurants)

scenes.say: The burgers just make sure the rent gets paid. Which is why
scenes.source: Paraphrase of the second half of the Sonneborn quote ('the greatest producer of revenue, from which our tenants can pay us our rent'), Wall Street Survivor

review_fix: Nov 13 review: hook changed to a 6-word claim, instant headline, trimmed from 57 s to ~45 s (popcorn at 62 s kept only 35% on average). Nov 14: bigword corrected from 1.9% to 1.4% to match the narration (Kroc kept 1.4% of the 1.9% fee).
